title: Dualizing objects compose along a closed immersion in the bounded-below etale comparison class
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell
e\operatorname{char}k$, and $A=A_{E,n}$ for a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}S$ be separated finite-type morphisms between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use the ordinary constant-$A$ module categories on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For $h=f,g,gf$, let $Rh_!$ be the compactification-independent etale compact-support functor [def-amb-etale-compact-support], and let $h^	imes$ be its ambient right adjoint. These adjoints preserve bounded-below complexes. The mate of the canonical bounded-below composition $Rg_!Rf_!\cong R(gf)_!$ is a natural isomorphism
$$ (gf)^	imes|_{D^+}\xrightarrow{\sim}f^	imes g^	imes|_{D^+}. $$
It identifies the composite counit with the pasted counits. For a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $a_W:W	o\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the structure maps for $W=T,Z$, so $a_Z=a_Ti$. Put $\omega_{W,e}=a_W^	imes A$. Its value at $A$ is the canonical counit-compatible identification $i^	imes\omega_{T,e}\cong\omega_{Z,e}$. Write $
u_W:W_{\mathrm{proet}}	o W_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the site-comparison morphism. Under $Rh_p^!=
u_X^*h^	imes R
u_{Y,*}$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] and the site-comparison unit, the same identification on etale-origin bounded-below objects gives $Ri_p^!\omega_{T,p}\cong\omega_{Z,p}$, where $\omega_{W,p}=Ra_{W,p}^!A$.

proof.text: Prepare the ordinary etale adjunctions. A field is Noetherian, so the finite-type-over-Noetherian lemma makes each of the schemes Noetherian; they are quasi-compact, and the locally-Noetherian quasi-separatedness lemma makes them quasi-separated. Nagata therefore gives a compactification $c_h=(j_h,p_h)$ for each $h=f,g,gf$. Here $p_h$ is proper, hence finite type. Finite-type composition makes its source $\overline X_h$ finite type over $k$. The finite-dimension lemma gives an integer $d_h\geq0$ with $\dim\overline X_h\leq d_h$ (take $d_h=0$ for an empty compactification). The ordinary etale exceptional-adjoint theorem supplies $F_h=Rp_{h,*}j_{h,!}\dashv h^\times$ on the unbounded ordinary etale categories. The same preparation applies to the structure maps below.

source.place: Tags 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), 01T3 (lemma-composition-finite-type); Nagata and finite-dimension inputs are the cited DAG statements.

proof.text: Verify the restriction of the right adjoint, without assuming its output is already bounded below. Write $S_V=\nu_V^*$ and $U_V=R\nu_{V,*}$. For $h:V\to W$ and $L\in D^+(W_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, the comparison unit $\eta_L:L\xrightarrow{\sim}U_WS_WL$ gives an isomorphism $S_Vh^\times L\cong S_Vh^\times U_WS_WL$. The right side is bounded below by clause 2 of thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class, since $S_WL$ is bounded below and the compactification bound $d_h$ was just checked. Exactness of $S_V$ gives $\mathcal H^r(S_Vh^\times L)=S_V\mathcal H^r(h^\times L)$. The functor $S_V$ detects zero module sheaves: a sheaf in degree zero is in $D^+$, where $S_V$ is fully faithful, so $S_VM=0$ forces $\operatorname{id}_M=0$. Thus the vanishing of the left side below a fixed degree implies the same vanishing for $h^\times L$. This proves $h^\times L\in D^+$.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.6 (bounded-below comparison unit), with the existing thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class clause 2; agent-written reflection argument using exactness on cohomology.

proof.text: The compact-support comparison theorem gives $\alpha:F_gF_f\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{gf}$ on $D^+$ and identifies the chosen-compactification candidates independently of refinements. Each $F_h$ preserves $D^+$: exact open extension is computed termwise, and the right derived proper direct image of a bounded-below complex is computed by a bounded-below injective resolution. Its ambient adjunction therefore restricts to the full $D^+$ categories, because both functors preserve this class. Apply the right-adjoint-composition lemma to these restricted adjunctions and the isomorphism $\alpha$. It gives the natural isomorphism $\theta:(gf)^\times|_{D^+}\xrightarrow{\sim}f^\times g^\times|_{D^+}$. Explicitly its Hom bijection is $\operatorname{Hom}(K,(gf)^\times L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_{gf}K,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_gF_fK,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(K,f^\times g^\times L)$. Thus it is exactly the mate of the specified composition map. Since these Hom bijections use the canonical compactification comparisons, their representing isomorphism is independent of the choices.

source.place: Bounded-below composition construction, followed by the formal adjunction composition of Stacks Tag 0DV0 (categories-lemma-compose-counits).

proof.text:
Write $\epsilon_h:F_hh^\times\to\operatorname{id}$ for the counits. The pasted-counit assertion of the right-adjoint-composition lemma gives, for every $L\in D^+$, the precise identity
$$\epsilon_{gf,L}\circ\alpha_{(gf)^\times L}=\epsilon_{g,L}\circ F_g(\epsilon_{f,g^\times L})\circ F_gF_f(\theta_L).$$
Both sides have source $F_gF_f(gf)^\times L$ and target $L$. Equivalently, first use $\alpha^{-1}$ to express the left functor as $F_gF_f$ and then use $\theta$ to express the right functor as $f^\times g^\times$; the counit becomes the two pasted counits. This also fixes the orientation of $\theta$.

proof.text: The closed-immersion properness lemma makes $i$ separated and finite type. Apply steps 1–4 to $Z\xrightarrow{i}T\xrightarrow{a_T}\operatorname{Spec}k$, whose composite is $a_Z$. The coefficient sheaf $A$ in degree zero belongs to $D^+$, so $\omega_{T,e}=a_T^\times A$ and $\omega_{Z,e}=a_Z^\times A$ are bounded below. Define $\kappa_e=\theta_A^{-1}:i^\times\omega_{T,e}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{Z,e}$. Evaluation of the identity in step 4 at $A$ proves its claimed counit compatibility. This is a specialization of the already constructed natural isomorphism and adds no purity or biduality premise.

proof.text:
Let $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and identify the constant pro-etale coefficient sheaf $A_p$ with $S_sA_e$; apply the canonical ring-sheaf identification in lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image to the geometric morphism $\nu_s$. From the finite formula in def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image and the comparison unit at $A_e$, obtain the explicit natural isomorphisms
$$\lambda_W:S_W\omega_{W,e}\xrightarrow{\ S_Wa_W^\times(\eta_{A_e})\ }S_Wa_W^\times U_sS_sA_e=\omega_{W,p}\qquad(W=T,Z).$$
For every $H\in D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ the same formula gives
$$\rho_H=S_Zi^\times(\eta_H):S_Zi^\times H\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri_p^!S_TH.$$
The unit is used only on the bounded-below etale objects $A_e,H$; all the displayed arrows are isomorphisms because functors preserve isomorphisms. In particular step 2 justifies their bounded-below codomains.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.6; explicit substitution into the finite formula of def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image, with constant-module pullback supplied by the cited lemma.

proof.text:
The required pro-etale identification is the following composite, so the site transport is fully specified:
$$Ri_p^!\omega_{T,p}\xrightarrow{Ri_p^!(\lambda_T^{-1})}Ri_p^!S_T\omega_{T,e}\xrightarrow{\rho_{\omega_{T,e}}^{-1}}S_Zi^\times\omega_{T,e}\xrightarrow{S_Z\kappa_e}S_Z\omega_{Z,e}\xrightarrow{\lambda_Z}\omega_{Z,p}.$$
Every factor is an isomorphism by steps 5–6. More generally for any $H\in D^+(s_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, replace $A_e$ everywhere by $H$ and use $\theta_H^{-1}$; the same formula gives the composition identification on etale-origin inputs. Naturality follows from the naturality of $\eta$, $\theta$ and functoriality. On Hom sets it inserts the comparison-unit isomorphisms into the restricted etale adjunction bijections of step 3, which are exactly the comparison-class bijections of thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class. Thus it is the same identification under site comparison, with the counit normalization inherited from step 4.
